item.description: ruin, devastation. “’S bochd an creachal a tha air m’inntinn.”
an altar boy.
a supportive person, e.g. a son / mother relationship.
pride. Specific reference to a son maintaining the family line by taking over from his father – “cumail pràthainn ’san teaghlach”.
a pub.
a root which was used for tanning. Cannot be more specific.
a miserly, tight-fisted person.
the playing of bagpipes. “Nuair a sheirmeadh a’ phìob.”
the noise of battle.
bits of cloth used as unconventional shoes. Fastened with strips of leather.
a Gaelic version of the word ‘puissant’, meaning domineering, having great power.
as in a fly or insect biting your skin. “Bha mi air mo chaobadh aig creilleagan.”
a bargain.
a general.
Dwelly used this for monuments but informant refers to Egypt as: “Ann an Eiphait nan carragh” – meaning pyramids.
refers to a horse being frightened or sidetracked during ploughing.
getting into mischief. “Chaidh mo chasan gu aimhleas.” – refers to the desire to dance after having one too many.
peeling of the skin as a result of excessive rubbing against something.
used as part of an expression indicating disbelief and amusement at what was being talked about. “O dhrongaireachd.”
some kind of soup, made from flesh.
splashes of mud sticking to your clothes as you run through a muddy field.
in reference to old, chubby, contented man – “Bodach seideanta”.
tossed about by the sea. “Nach iad a fhuair an cuanluasgadh.”
I think this could mean lashing or striking? “’S earball an casadh ri dhruim.”
a sharp pain.
shining.
large heaps of seaweed. Also in the sense of a bulky woman.
in the sense of a strong striding action. “Chan fhaca mi riamh te bha cho strapail gu coiseachd.”
as in a person being messed up, e.g. being subjected to having mud thrown at him – “Bha mi air mo pheabladh.” A useful word in connection with traditional activities at ‘stag’ nights.
a covering or layer. Similar to ‘sgrath’.
mean, stingy. In reference to landlords. “B’e sud na h-uachdrain mhaoidhteach.”
a short walk.
as appears in traditional panegyric description of a chief or appropriate person. Refers to large and muscular thighs.
modestly, kindly, e.g. “Dhiult mi le deachainneachd an oifis sin a ghabhail.”
a thin veil of clouds which hide the sun – “A’ ghrian fo sgiobal nan nial”.
a hat without a hollow in its top – “Ad gun tolg”.
stained.
hooligans, thugs. “Fhuair e droch liodraigeadh measg nan umaidh air sràidean Ghlaschu.”
well-built or developed. “Each triamanta.”
undisturbed. “Cadal loisinneach.”
little glens on croft land.
romantic association. “Na daoine ris an robh mi guaineis.”
e.g. haystacks bulging with hay. “B’e foghar a bh’ann a dh’fhàg buchd nam chruachan.” Could this mean bulk?
an ounce of sense. “Chan eil rocag aig an duin’ ud.”
cannot make anything of it. “Cha dean mi stém dheth.”
steadfast. “’Se duine stagant a bh’ann an Dùghall.”
this word came up in context of a pipe used for smoking. Not precisely sure but informant thinks it could be the lid of the pipe. “Agus spidean air a màs.” Personally not convinced about this.
tummers of a boat having been steamed and shaped. “Farachan cruinn de mhaide.”
to dip, bathe.
[See fatradh.]
trustworthy, dependable.
to beat up, knock about. Similar to ‘liodraigeadh’.
a cup which has been chipped – “Bha peasgadh air.”
a dance or other similar function. “Bheil thu dol gu soiree a nochd?”
fastenings.
an expression similar to ‘my love’ in English. “Seadh a’ cheist dè ni mi dhut an diugh.”
threatening overhead conditions with rain clouds about to break.
a spray or hail of rain.
